name: opencode-plugin-api-v2
body:
The apg opencode tool suite runs as an opencode 2.x plugin. Each suite tool file under `opencode-suite/tools/` default-exports a plugin definition — `Plugin.define({ id, setup(ctx) })` imported from `@opencode/plugin` — whose `setup` registers its one tool through a synchronous `ctx.tool.transform(editor => editor.add({ name, description, input, options, execute }))`. The registered tool carries a name, a description, a JSON-Schema `input` object, and an `execute(input, context)` that returns structured content (`{ content }`). Each tool keeps its own file and its own import of the shared lib, so the suite holds one plugin per tool file; each plugin's `id` is its tool's effective name (for example `apg_query`, `apg_rm`), unique across the suite because tool names are unique.

The shared lib `opencode-suite/lib/apg.ts` sources the plugin's load location from the opencode 2.x plugin context — `ctx.location.directory` and `ctx.location.project` — and a tool's own optional `directory` argument stays the authoritative project directory (the base the curated tools rebase stored repo-relative identities onto, `requirements.requirement.absolute-paths-at-tool-boundary`). The plugins close over their `setup(ctx)` context for the location.

The filesystem tools (`apg_rm`, `apg_mv`, `apg_cp`) keep their operations confined to the acting agent's granted globs under the opencode 2.x `permissions` model (`requirements.requirement.agent-fs-write-operations`, `requirements.requirement.code-writer-worktree-only-writes`), and the pure `ts.apg-opencode-suite.lib.apg.fsScopeDecision` boundary-and-ordered-match decision stays the same. The way a tool learns the acting agent's identity and effective `permissions` rules under 2.x is the accepted open item of `requirements.constraint.agent-fs-per-path-permission`, verified by unit/int tests against a faked V2 tool context with real-runtime verification outside this change-set. An unresolvable acting agent refuses every path (fail-closed).

Acceptance criteria: every `opencode-suite/tools/*.ts` file imports `Plugin` from `@opencode/plugin` and default-exports `Plugin.define({ id, setup })`; `setup` registers its tool through `ctx.tool.transform` with a JSON-Schema `input` and an `execute` returning `{ content }`; each plugin `id` is unique across the suite and is its tool's effective name; `opencode-suite/lib/apg.ts` sources the load location from the opencode 2.x plugin context; `opencode-suite/package.json` depends on `@opencode/plugin`; the fs tools keep their operations inside the acting agent's granted globs under the 2.x `permissions` model and the pure `fsScopeDecision` semantics are unchanged; the acting-agent-identity mechanism is stated as the accepted open item verified against a faked V2 tool context.
